code_actions.rationale: Policy requires explicit provider documentation of anoxic brain injury or the presumption criteria; neurology documents encouraging exam and neuroprognostication consistent with intact function and the discharge summary documents excellent neurologic recovery rather than established anoxic brain damage. No clear physician assessment meeting G93.1 criteria was found.

TTE documents preserved LV ejection fraction and isolated RV dysfunction consistent with PE; there is no physician documentation of diastolic congestive heart failure in the assessment or discharge. The code is not supported by imaging/assessment.

Objective data (high PCT, lactate, vasopressors) suggest possible septic physiology (ev_0003) but I could not find explicit physician documentation or discharge diagnosis of severe sepsis/septic shock in the attending assessment or discharge summary (ev_0005). Provider adjudication requested (HITL).
Nursing documentation explicitly states No renal replacement required; AKI improving and there is no physician documentation of RRT initiation. The billed urinary filtration code is unsupported.

discharge_disposition: 62 - Discharged/transferred to an inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF)

evidence.quote: CT pulmonary angiography confirmed massive bilateral saddle pulmonary embolism with right heart strain.
Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after 15 minutes of CPR with three defibrillation attempts and multiple rounds of ACLS medications.
ABG (02:00): pH 7.29 / PaCO2 44 / PaO2 66 / HCO3 20; lactate 5.0 mmol/L; P/F ratio 69.
Post-arrest patient with encouraging early neurologic exam. Neuroprognostication at 72 hours indicated intact function with follow-up expected excellent.

Resolved massive pulmonary embolism status post catheter-directed thrombolysis; resolved cardiac arrest with successful ROSC; excellent neurologic recovery post-arrest; resolved right ventricular dysfunction; resolved AKI; right common femoral DVT on anticoagulation; IVC filter in place; hypothyroidism; depression; ICU-acquired weakness.
No renal replacement required; AKI improving.
Admitting Dx Massive pulmonary embolism with cardiac arrest and successful resuscitation

policy_citations.document: Policy Documents/DRG/Massive Pulmonary Embolism with Acute Cor Pulmonale.docx
policy_citations.quote: 1. Criterion 1 — Provider Documentation: Provider documentation of 'massive pulmonary embolism,' 'high-risk pulmonary embolism,' 'pulmonary embolism with acute cor pulmonale,' or 'pulmonary embolism with right heart strain/right ventricular dysfunction' as a confirmed diagnosis in the provider's assessment, cardiology or pulmonology consultation note, critical care note, or discharge summary.

1. Criterion 1 — Provider Documentation of Diagnosis: Provider documentation of anoxic brain injury, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, post-cardiac arrest brain injury, or hypoxic brain damage as a clinically established diagnosis in the assessment or problem list, explicitly attributing neurological injury to the qualifying hypoxic or anoxic event.

system_note: Summary of what was billed: Principal diagnosis I26.09 (Other pulmonary embolism with acute cor pulmonale) and multiple MCC/CC comorbidities were billed, including I46.9 (cardiac arrest), G93.1 (anoxic brain damage), J96.01 (acute respiratory failure w/ hypoxia), I50.30 (diastolic CHF), N17.9 (AKI), I82.401 (RLE DVT), R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock). Key procedures billed include catheter-directed pulmonary interventions and an IVC device, plus an RRT code (5A1D80Z). What the record documents (selected, source/section/page): - Massive bilateral saddle pulmonary embolism with right heart strain; catheter-directed thrombolysis performed (History & Physical (Admitting), p.474) [evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n9]. - CT pulmonary angiography: Massive bilateral pulmonary artery embolism with hemodynamic significance (Diagnostic Imaging Report - CTPA, p.17) [evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n13]. - Transthoracic echo: Right ventricular dilation with severe hypokinesis; left ventricular ejection fraction preserved - findings consistent with acute right heart strain from massive PE (TTE report, p.17) [evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n14]. - Out-of-hospital pulseless VT arrest with ROSC after 15 minutes; admitted to CVICU and treated with TTM and catheter-directed thrombolysis (History & Physical, p.474; Critical Care Progress Note p.162) [evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n9; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n11]. - Patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated with ABG showing PaO2 66 on high FiO2 and P/F ratio ~69 (Critical Care Progress Note, p.162) supporting acute hypoxemic respiratory failure [evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n11]. - Problem list / discharge documentation shows right common femoral DVT discovered during stay and IVC filter placed (H&P problem list p.117; Discharge/Transfer Summary p.833) [evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n9; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n971]. Primary coding-policy tests applied (selected): - I26.09 policy requires (1) provider documentation of massive/high-risk PE or PE with RV strain, (2) radiographic confirmation of PE (CTPA), and (3) hemodynamic instability (vasopressors or cardiac arrest) or objective RV dysfunction; catheter-directed thrombolysis or other high-risk PE management also supports the code (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Massive-Pulmonary-Embolism-with-Acute-Cor-Pulmonale.docx). - I46.9 policy requires documentation of pulseless arrest and ROSC; sequencing depends on whether the arrest or its precipitant occasioned the admission (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx). - G93.1 policy requires explicit provider attribution to anoxic/hypoxic brain injury (or the presumption rule when post-arrest coma persisting beyond 24 hrs off sedation with neuroprognostication initiated) (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Anoxic-Brain-Injury.docx). How I applied the three-way check and the conclusions (with explicit evidence citations): 1) I26.09 (principal): supported. The H&P states the patient collapsed from massive bilateral saddle PE and documents catheter-directed thrombolysis and RV strain on imaging (History & Physical, p.474) [ev_0001], the diagnostic CT is positive for massive saddle PE (Diagnostic Imaging Report - CTPA, p.17), and the TTE documents severe RV dysfunction (TTE, p.17). The I26.09 validation criteria (provider documentation + imaging + hemodynamic instability/cardiac arrest or objective RV dysfunction) are met (policy: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Massive-Pulmonary-Embolism-with-Acute-Cor-Pulmonale.docx-b29, b31, b36-b41) [pol_001]. Therefore sequencing I26.09 as principal is supported by the record (H&P and Facesheet show PE as the precipitant) [ev_0008; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_07.pdf-n4]. 2) I46.9 (cardiac arrest): supported as an additional diagnosis (MCC). The chart documents an out-of-hospital pulseless VT arrest with ROSC after 15 minutes (History & Physical, p.474) satisfying the arrest documentation and ROSC requirement (Critical Care Progress Note also documents arrest/ROSC) [ev_0002]. Per policy, when the precipitating condition (here PE) is clearly identified as the cause of arrest and the admission documentation frames PE as the reason for presentation, sequencing the PE principal with cardiac arrest secondary is acceptable (policy gives guidance to auditor to use clinical documentation) [pol_001; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Cardiac-Arrest-with-Return-of-Spontaneous-Circulation.docx-b52-b55]. 3) J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia): supported (MCC). The patient was intubated/mechanically ventilated and ABG/pulse-oximetry values show severe hypoxemia (ABG PaO2 66, P/F ≈ 69) documented in the critical care note, and the provider documents respiratory failure with mechanical ventilation and lung protective settings (Critical Care Progress Note, p.162) [ev_0003]. Policy presumption rules allow J96.01 when invasive mechanical ventilation is initiated and attributed to acute respiratory failure [RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b36] (policy row used in review). 4) G93.1 (anoxic brain damage): NOT supported as billed. The G93.1 policy requires provider documentation explicitly calling the injury anoxic brain injury / hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy / post-cardiac arrest brain injury or presumption criteria (persistent coma beyond 24 hours off sedation with neuroprognostication started) to validate the code (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Anoxic-Brain-Injury.docx-b30-b31) [pol_002]. Here the neurology note documents an encouraging early neurologic exam and that neuroprognostication at 72 hours was consistent with intact function and expected excellent recovery (Neurology Consultation, p.604) [ev_0004]; the Discharge/Transfer Summary documents excellent neurologic recovery post-arrest (Transfer/Discharge Summary, p.833) [ev_0005]. There is no clear provider assessment in the record explicitly diagnosing anoxic brain damage / hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (G93.1) - instead the documentation documents post-arrest care, TTM, and eventual neurologic recovery. Under the policy language that requires explicit provider attribution (or the presumption of anoxic injury only when a post-arrest coma persists off sedation with formal prognostication), the record does not meet G93.1 validation. Therefore G93.1 should be removed. Evidence: policy (G93.1 criterion 1) and neurology/discharge notes showing recovery rather than established anoxic injury [pol_002, ev_0004, ev_0005]. 5) I50.30 (unspecified diastolic CHF): NOT supported. The TTE documents preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and describes right ventricular dilation/hypokinesis consistent with acute right heart strain from PE (TTE report, p.17) [ / ev_0006]. The problem list and discharge narrative describe right ventricular failure with recovery, not left-sided diastolic congestive heart failure. There is no provider statement diagnosing congestive diastolic heart failure in the admission or discharge documentation. Therefore I50.30 is not supported and should be removed. 6) N17.9 (AKI): supported as CC. The H&P documents post-arrest AKI (KDIGO 2) with elevated creatinine early in the course and a recovery by discharge (H&P and Discharge Summary) - this meets N17.9 criteria (History & Physical problem list; Discharge Summary p.833) [ev_0001; ev_0005]. 7) I82.401 (acute DVT, right lower extremity): supported (POA=N). The H&P/problem list and discharge indicate a provoked right common femoral DVT identified after admission and managed with IVC filter placement and anticoagulation (H&P problem list; Discharge/Transfer Summary) [ev_0001; ev_0005; ev_0007]. POA=N is consistent with the event developing during the encounter. 8) R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock): UNCERTAIN / borderline documentation. The chart shows marked inflammatory markers (very high procalcitonin and CRP), lactate elevation, and vasopressor use documented in the critical care progress notes (Critical Care Progress Note, p.162) [ev_0003]. However, I did not find a clear provider assessment line explicitly documenting "severe sepsis" or "septic shock" in the physician-authored assessment/active problem entries or in the discharge diagnoses (the Discharge/Transfer Summary does not list sepsis among discharge diagnoses) [ev_0005]. Because coding for sepsis generally requires provider attribution (and the retrieved records are mixed: objective markers + treatment present but no explicit provider diagnosis), I flag this item for human review (see HITL question below) rather than making a unilateral change. 9) Procedure 5A1D80Z (urinary filtration / RRT): remove. Nursing documentation explicitly states No renal replacement required; AKI improving during the ICU course (Nursing Progress Note - Evening Shift, p.422) [ev_0007], and the Problem List / Discharge Summary indicate AKI that recovered without dialysis and no documentation of renal replacement therapy initiation. The record therefore contradicts the billed RRT procedure. 10) Procedures corresponding to catheter-directed thrombolysis and IVC filter placement are documented (H&P and procedure/IR notes) and are supported (evidence: History & Physical and Discharge Summary; CT/Interventional note) [ev_0001; ; ev_0008]. Net action taken (claim-level): Remove the unsupported diagnosis codes G93.1 and I50.30 and remove the unsupported procedure 5A1D80Z (performance of urinary filtration). Leave other billed diagnoses and procedures in place, except hold R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) for human adjudication because objective data suggest possible sepsis but provider attribution is not explicit in the physician assessment or discharge diagnoses. References (verbatim passages used): ev_0001-ev_0009 below. Recommended corrected billing lists (complete corrected sets after removing unsupported items): - Revised diagnosis list (position 1 = principal): [ "I26.09", "I46.9", "J96.01", "N17.9", "I82.401", "E03.9", "F32.9", "Z86.73", "Z79.01", "Z95.81" ] - Revised procedure list (ICD-10-PCS codes): [ "0BH17EZ", "02JYXZZ", "06H03DZ", "027Q3ZZ", "3E043GC", "02HV33Z", "03HY32Z", "5A2204Z" ] (removed 5A1D80Z) Audit actions taken: claim-level Finding due to unsupported diagnoses/procedure described above. See code_decisions for line-by-line actions and evidence IDs.
rationale_letter: Re: Clinical validation audit - inpatient stay MR_07 This office reviewed the medical record and coding for the inpatient admission beginning 03/13/2026 (claim MR_07). The audit compared what was billed to the medical record documentation and to the governing coding validation policies for the targeted conditions. Findings: - I26.09 (Other pulmonary embolism with acute cor pulmonale) - upheld as the principal diagnosis. Basis: CT angiography confirmed a massive bilateral saddle pulmonary embolism with hemodynamic significance and the admitting H&P documents right heart strain and catheter-directed thrombolysis (History & Physical (Admitting), p.474; Diagnostic Imaging Report - CTPA, p.17) [evidence: ev_0001; ]. Bedside transthoracic echo documented severe right ventricular dilation/hypokinesis (TTE, p.17) supporting acute cor pulmonale. Under the I26.09 validation criteria, provider documentation + imaging + hemodynamic compromise (including cardiac arrest) meet the policy requirements (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Massive-Pulmonary-Embolism-with-Acute-Cor-Pulmonale). - I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) - upheld as a secondary diagnosis (MCC). Basis: The chart documents an out-of-hospital pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest with return of spontaneous circulation after 15 minutes of CPR and defibrillation (History & Physical; Critical Care Progress Note) (ev_0002). - J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) - upheld (MCC). Basis: The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated with ABG/P/F evidence of severe hypoxemia (Critical Care Progress Note shows PaO2 66 and P/F ≈69) and provider documentation attributes need for invasive ventilation to respiratory failure (ev_0003). - G93.1 (Anoxic brain damage) - NOT supported; removed. Basis: G93.1 requires explicit provider documentation of anoxic brain injury or presumption criteria (policy: RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Anoxic-Brain-Injury). Here neurology documented an encouraging neurologic exam and neuroprognostication consistent with intact function and the Discharge Summary documents excellent neurologic recovery (Neurology Consultation, p.604; Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.833) (ev_0004; ev_0005). I found no physician-authored assessment explicitly diagnosing anoxic brain damage or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy that would satisfy the policy criteria (pol_002). Therefore the code G93.1 is not supported by the documentation and is removed. - I50.30 (Unspecified diastolic congestive heart failure) - NOT supported; removed. Basis: Cardiac imaging documents preserved LV ejection fraction and isolated acute right ventricular dysfunction consistent with PE (TTE, p.17) (/ev_0006); there is no provider diagnosis of diastolic CHF in the clinician assessment or discharge diagnoses. - N17.9 (Acute kidney failure) - upheld (CC). Basis: Provider problem list and course document post-arrest AKI with objective creatinine changes and conservative management with recovery by discharge (ev_0001; ev_0005). - I82.401 and Z95.81 (right-sided DVT and IVC filter) - upheld; documentation shows provoked right common femoral DVT identified during the encounter and IVC filter placed (ev_0001; ev_0007). - 5A1D80Z (Performance of urinary filtration / RRT) - NOT supported; removed. Basis: Nursing documentation and problem/course notes explicitly state No renal replacement required; AKI improving (Nursing Progress Note - Evening Shift, p.422) and no RRT initiation appears in the physician operative/medication records (ev_0007). - R65.21 (Severe sepsis with septic shock) - unresolved at auditor level. Basis: Objective data (very high procalcitonin, lactate, vasopressor use) suggest infection and shock were treated; however I did not find a clear physician assessment or discharge diagnosis explicitly documenting "severe sepsis" or "septic shock." Because sepsis coding requires provider attribution, I request clinician adjudication: please confirm whether the attending physician(s) intended and documented severe sepsis / septic shock as an active diagnosis on this encounter (see HITL question below). Correction made to the claim: G93.1 and I50.30 removed from the diagnosis list; 5A1D80Z removed from the procedure list. The remaining diagnoses and procedures are left as billed except R65.21, which requires provider adjudication. If you agree that the attending intended severe sepsis with septic shock and will provide an explicit physician note to that effect, R65.21 may be retained; otherwise it should be removed. Thank you for your attention. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team
